true_positive_cat1_modbus_len3_signature.explanation: Detected with near-unity score by all models (A, B, C, D) due to the repeated func_code=5, modbus_len=3, packet_size=75 response frames.

positive_cat2_non_shortcut_quantity_scan.explanation: Contains reconnaissance requests with abnormal register quantities (quantity in {2,4,5,9,20,125,2000,65535}) and modbus_len=6 rather than modbus_len=3.

positive_cat3_event_mapped_normal_protoc.example_role: Hard Positive / False Negative (Category 3: event_mapped read/response window)
positive_cat3_event_mapped_normal_protoc.explanation: Packets in this window have routine protocol fields (func_code in {1..4}, modbus_len in {9,10,11}, register_start=0, quantity in {0,1}) identical to normal polling, labelled positive only via timestamp proximity to attack_events_mapped.

true_negative_routine_polling.explanation: Standard cyclic Modbus/TCP polling sequence with regular inter-request timing and normal frame lengths.

highest_scoring_normal_window_fp_analysi.example_role: Borderline / Highest-Scoring Normal Window (False Positive Analysis)
highest_scoring_normal_window_fp_analysi.explanation: Normal window with the highest out-of-fold LSTM score, illustrating how unusual timing bursts or function-code transitions can elevate the anomaly score.

lowest_scoring_positive_window_fn_analys.explanation: Positive window where only a single packet at the boundary carries a label and protocol fields match normal polling.
